reviews.body: Fine for now, see the thread about the HTTP library.

comments.author: carol
comments.body: Question more than a request: we already get httpx through the FastAPI test client. Is there a reason to pull in `requests` too, or should the clients all standardise on one library?

comments.author: dan
comments.body: Honestly just habit, `requests` is what I know. Happy to switch if we have a preference.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: requests is fine for now. This is one GET against a status page with a timeout, it can't hurt anything. We'll standardise outbound HTTP later: fraud scoring and FX are both coming this quarter, and I'd rather design one shared client with timeouts, retries and metrics once we know what those need than guess now. Leave it as is.

comments.author: dan
comments.body: Ok, leaving it. Timeout is already set to 3s.

comments.author: frank
comments.body: Please add a docstring here explaining the fallback behaviour. Every function should say what it does, especially when it silently maps unknown values to something else.

comments.author: carol
comments.body: I'd skip it. Private helpers are documented by their names, and this one is five lines you can read in one glance. We only put docstrings on the public service functions, otherwise they rot the first time someone edits the helper. The fallback is covered by the second test, which is a better description than a docstring anyway.

comments.author: frank
comments.body: Not how I'd do it, but it's your codebase.

threads.rejection_reason: Private helpers are documented by their names; we only document public service functions.
